key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that morphology and optoelectronic quality can decouple.
engineering_relevance: Capping layers could help preserve uniform optoelectronic performance during aging, so surface smoothness alone should not determine perovskite film quality.
method: Form mixed-dimensional heterostructures using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium-derived Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare capped and pristine films before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative QFLS, with homogeneity largely preserved during accelerated aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not report device efficiency, quantitative effect sizes, or aging conditions, limiting assessment of photovoltaic-scale durability.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
